pr.title: Name everything the build needs before the installer stops (install.md chunk 5)
pr.head: a048abf3652a38bbbb692f40e03f9e9a5bdd785e

summary: install.sh is Field's one installer. Run inside a checkout, it installs that checkout. Piped from curl, or downloaded by field upgrade, it installs a release. Either way it builds the CLI with pnpm and the audio daemon field-audiod with CMake, which downloads and compiles the JUCE framework. Before it builds, it checks for the tools the build needs.

Before this change, those checks stopped at the first missing tool, so a new machine took one run per tool. They also never looked for a C++ compiler, git, or the Linux development headers JUCE compiles against, so a machine without them failed minutes into the JUCE build. Most people meet this on the one-line install, on a machine that has never built Field.

Now every check the target needs runs first. Each missing or old tool adds a labeled row and what supplies it: a Homebrew formula on macOS, a Debian or Ubuntu package on Linux, or a manual step where no package fits. The installer then prints every row, one brew install or sudo apt-get install line, the manual steps, and the command to run again. It exits 69 before it downloads, builds, or links anything, and it installs nothing itself. Offering to run the Homebrew command is chunk 6, which the plan describes and nobody has started.

cards.title: What the review found
cards.html:
• Two open findings, both about Linux remedies. The only pnpm step, corepack enable pnpm, fails on Node 25 and newer, which ship no Corepack. A missing CMake gets the apt cmake package, which on Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 11 is older than 3.24, so the next run asks again.
  • Two suggestions. Check make on Linux, which CMake's default generator needs. Drop the manual-step strings that need can never print.
  • What ran. Typecheck, project check, bash -n, the installer's 86 tests, and sandboxed runs with a stubbed PATH and a temporary HOME. CI passes on this head.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Row. One line of the report: a label such as cmake-missing, then what Field needs.
  • Formula. A Homebrew package, installed with brew install.
  • Xcode command line tools. Apple's compiler, git, and make, which xcode-select --install installs and xcode-select -p locates.
  • pkg-config module. The name under which a library's development files register, such as alsa or x11. JUCE's CMake finds its Linux libraries through them.
  • Exit status 69. EX_UNAVAILABLE from sysexits.h. Every missing-prerequisite stop in the installer uses it.

groups.title: Every check runs before the installer stops
groups.kicker: install.sh: the check functions, the collector, and the one report
intro: Each prerequisite has a check_ function: check_node, check_pnpm, check_cmake, check_compiler, check_git, check_headers, and check_fetch for curl and tar. A check that finds a tool missing or too old no longer stops the script. It calls need, which adds a row to the report and puts the remedy on one of three lists: BREW for Homebrew formulae on macOS, APT for Debian and Ubuntu packages elsewhere, or STEPS for a manual line when the platform has no package for that row.

require_tools takes the names of the checks a target needs and runs them all. When any added a row, it prints the report to stderr and exits 69. Each target in checkout_main and release_main now calls it once, in place of the separate require_node, require_pnpm, require_cmake, and require_fetch_tools calls, which this change removes.

Two checks are new in kind. On macOS, the compiler and git come from Xcode's command line tools, and /usr/bin/c++ and /usr/bin/git exist even without them, as stubs that open an install dialog. So check_compiler asks xcode-select -p for the tools' directory instead of running either. On Linux, check_headers asks pkg-config for each module the JUCE build links. Without pkg-config it cannot look, so it names pkg-config and every header package.

checks.text: OS is read once from uname -s when the script loads. The macOS checks run when it is Darwin, the header check only when it is Linux, and every other system gets the apt names with a line saying to translate them when apt-get is absent.

files.note: The new checks, need and require_tools, and each target's single call to require_tools.

checks.text: need picks one remedy per row. On macOS a row with a formula goes on the brew install line. Elsewhere a row with an apt package goes on the apt-get line. Only a row with neither prints its manual step.

Open finding: on Linux the only pnpm step is corepack enable pnpm, but Node.js stopped distributing Corepack in 25.0.0. A machine with Node 25 or 26 and no pnpm passes check_node, and the printed step fails with corepack: command not found. The base also named https://pnpm.io/installation, and the status row at line 426 still does. Keep a step that works without Corepack beside it.

Open finding: a missing CMake on Linux gets the apt cmake package, which is CMake 3.22.1 on Ubuntu 22.04 and 3.18.4 on Debian 11, both below 3.24. The next run then reports cmake-old and only then names cmake.org. Print the cmake.org step for a missing CMake on Linux too, in place of the package or beside it.

With the xcode-select stand-in removed, a macOS-mode run lists xcode-missing and prints xcode-select --install before the Homebrew lines. The test at src/install.test.ts:490 asserts that order, and it passes. The check never runs /usr/bin/c++ or /usr/bin/git.

The Linux compiler check does not look for make, which CMake's default generator needs. A compiler installed without build-essential, beside a CMake from cmake.org, passes every check and then fails at configure. The base had the same gap, and the review lists it as a suggestion.

HEADER_PACKAGES holds the same eleven packages, in the same order, that .github/workflows/ci.yml installs before pnpm build:native on Ubuntu. CI's comment says that list came from what a bare ubuntu:24.04 container needed. Compared against ci.yml at this head.

Every check_ function returns 0 on every path, and every need call passes all five arguments. So under set -euo pipefail the loop runs every check to the end and no unset argument stops it. Traced by reading each function at this head.
Every sandboxed run that found something missing exited 69 and left the temporary HOME empty. The runs covered release mode on Linux and macOS, with the targets all, cli, and audiod.

A release all also checks curl and tar. require_shim_free runs after require_tools, so a field that belongs to something else in the bin directory shows up only on the run after the tools are in place.

groups.title: Tests stub the platform and every tool
groups.kicker: src/install.test.ts: uname, xcode-select, c++, and pkg-config become stand-ins
intro: The installer's tests run the real install.sh under bash, with HOME set to a fresh temporary directory and PATH limited to a directory of links and stand-ins. So nothing installed on the machine can answer for a missing tool. This change adds four stand-ins. uname reports FAKE_UNAME for uname -s, so the macOS and Linux checks both run wherever the suite runs. xcode-select prints a directory that exists, c++ does nothing, and pkg-config finds every module except those FAKE_NO_HEADERS names. A test removes a stand-in to make a tool missing.

The new install.sh before it changes anything block covers everything missing at once on macOS, one missing formula with Homebrew present, several misses on Linux, a Linux without apt-get, a Linux without pkg-config, and a macOS without pkg-config, where no header check runs. A release-mode test removes curl and tar and checks that the data directory was never made.

files.note: Four new stand-ins, platform-specific pnpm tests, and a block for the combined report.

checks.text: All 86 tests in this file pass at this head under macOS's bash 3.2, and CI's linux job ran them under bash 5. No field-install-* directory was left in the temporary directory afterward.
The uname stand-in answers only uname -s and hands every other call to the real uname. install_audiod and profile_hint also call uname -s, so they see the faked platform too.
This test asserts the order of the steps: xcode-select --install comes before the Homebrew lines, because Homebrew needs the command line tools too.
The stand-ins answer the same on every distribution, so no test can show the two Linux findings: a Node without Corepack, or a distribution whose CMake package is older than 3.24.

groups.title: Documentation and the plan
groups.kicker: docs/install.md shows the report; the install plan adds §3.4 and chunks 5 and 6
intro: docs/install.md replaced its list of what the installer does not check with an example of the new report. It now lists what each target needs, with the platform's remedy beside each tool. The install plan adds §3.4, which states the problem and describes chunk 5, this change, and chunk 6, which would offer to run the Homebrew command. It adds acceptance criteria for both and marks chunks 3 and 4 shipped.

The plan is in-progress at both the base and the head, so this change flips no status, and its new text leaves no question open. §7.4, which domain serves the installer, still reads as an open question, although chunk 4 shipped on field.one.

files.note: "Before you install" now shows the report and lists each target's needs.

checks.text: The example matches, byte for byte, the stderr of a macOS-mode release run with no Node, pnpm, CMake, or Homebrew in a sandbox.
What each target needs here matches the require_tools calls in checkout_main and release_main: audiod skips Node, curl, and tar, cli checks Node and pnpm, and workers checks Node alone.
This bullet gives the same single pnpm step as the open finding at install.sh:162, so the fix there applies here too.

files.note: §2.2 now says every check runs first; §3.4, the chunk 5 and 6 criteria, and §6 are new or updated.

checks.text: §3.4 holds the design for both chunks. Chunk 6 asks before it runs brew install, reads the answer from /dev/tty because bash reads the script itself from stdin, and keeps xcode-select --install as a printed step because it returns before the tools are installed.
The code meets both chunk 5 criteria on macOS. On Linux the first one, which says the printed commands install what is missing, fails in the two cases the open findings describe.

§6 now records chunk 4 as shipped on field.one, but §7.4, which domain serves the installer, still reads as open. The question predates this change. install.sh and docs/install.md still name the raw.githubusercontent.com URL that field.one proxies, so no code depends on the domain.
